item.title: Bevy 0.20：实时路径追踪器 Solari 上 Metal、画质更准，ReSTIR 反而默认关掉了
item.description:
一句话：ReSTIR 改进让渲染基本无偏，但吃性能多、收益小，于是改成可选并默认关闭，改用 DLSS-RR 撑性能。

要点：

  • Solari（实时路径追踪插件）改进 ReSTIR 后渲染基本无偏、光照更准；移动物体的阴影不再滞后，非金属材质运动时反射不再闪
  • DLSS-RR 变好之后，ReSTIR 在很多场景吃掉可观性能却提升有限，因此改为可选、默认关闭，需要时用 SolariLighting::restir 重新打开
  • 着色器语言转向 WESL（WGSL 的标准化扩展）并成为官方方案；Sprite 可写自定义着色器材质，2D 材质也能像 3D 一样扩展；本版 227 位贡献者、817 个 PR

为什么值得看：「宁可关掉一个先进特性也要换来帧率」是引擎工程的常态判断，这次的公开理由（改进后收益不再抵得上成本）值得作为性能取舍的案例看。

中文摘要：Bevy 0.20 的核心变化在渲染：实时路径追踪插件 Solari 的多个方面都有大幅改进，ReSTIR 实现改善后渲染基本无偏、光照更准确，移动物体的阴影不再滞后，非金属材质在运动中的反射也不再闪烁；在 macOS 上通过 Metal 也能运行。性能方面，由于 DLSS-RR 近期进步明显，而 ReSTIR 在不少场景中占用可观性能却对画质提升有限，团队把它改为可选并默认关闭，若仍需要可显式开启 SolariLighting::restir。此外 Bevy 正式采用 WESL 作为着色器语言，Sprite 支持自定义着色器材质、2D 材质可像 3D 一样扩展，Feathers UI 增加多个控件，版本由 227 位贡献者的 817 个 PR 组成。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：Bevy（中文）

原文发布：2026-10-08

本期推送：2026-10-24

Bevy 0.20

Posted on October 8, 2026 by Bevy Contributors

The Zorah scene rendered in Bevy Solari

Thanks to 227 contributors, 817 pull requests, community reviewers, and our generous donors, we're happy to announce the Bevy 0.20 release on crates.io!

For those who don't know, Bevy is a refreshingly simple data-driven game engine built in Rust. You can check out our Quick Start Guide to try it today. It's free and open source forever! You can grab the full source code on GitHub. Check out Bevy Assets for a collection of community-developed plugins, games, and learning resources.

To update an existing Bevy App or Plugin to Bevy 0.20, check out our 0.19 to 0.20 Migration Guide.

Since our last release a few months ago we've added a ton of new features, bug fixes, and quality of life tweaks, but here are some of the highlights:

  • Solari and DLSS: Solari, Bevy's realtime pathtraced renderer, is now faster, more accurate, supports more Bevy rendering features, and runs on macOS via Metal!
  • BSN Syntax Improvements: BSN, Bevy's new scene system, had some syntax changes that made it much easier to read and compose
  • Ready Event: BSN scene entities now trigger an observable 
    Ready
     event when all of their children have been spawned.
  • More UI Widgets: Bevy Feathers, Bevy's opinionated editor-centric UI toolkit, now has Color Input, Scrollable List View, Dropdown Selection, and Lazy Menu widgets. The Number Input widget is now scrubbable / draggable, and we've added Headless Tab Widgets.
  • WESL Shaders: Bevy has officially adopted the WESL shader language (a standardized extension of WGSL). WESL is already an improvement over Bevy's old custom WGSL dialect, and we've been working with the WESL team to plan out the future of shader development in Bevy.
  • Sprite Materials and Extended 2D Materials: It is now possible to create custom shader materials for Sprites, and 2D mesh materials can now be extended like they can in 3D.
  • Pan Orbit Camera: Bevy now has a "pan orbit camera", making it possible to navigate scenes in a CAD-like way.

    • Solari and DLSS #

    Authors:@JMS55, @mate-h, @stuartparmenterPRs:#24667, #24767, #25082, #25123, #25244, #25423, #25513, #25518, #25703, #25704, #25787, #25814

    Solari, Bevy's realtime pathtraced renderer, has seen major improvements to pretty much every aspect of the plugin!

    Read JMS55's blog for the technical details, or continue reading below for the high level overview.

    Improved Image Quality #

    Thanks to improvements in our ReSTIR implementation, rendering is now mostly unbiased, leading to much more accurate lighting.

    Additionally, thanks to some other changes, moving objects no longer have shadows that lag behind, and reflections now look significantly less shimmery in motion, especially for non-metallic materials.

    Improved Performance #

    DLSS-RR has gotten very good in recent updates, and for many scenes, ReSTIR costs a decent chunk of performance, and does not significantly improve image quality.

    As a result, we've decided to make ReSTIR optional, and turn it off by default.

    If you were using Solari in Bevy 0.19, check if the loss of ReSTIR affects your scene, and if so re-enable 

    SolariLighting::restir
    .

    With ReSTIR off, expect reduced shadow quality and missing shadows in motion in scenes with many lights. We are exploring cheaper ways of improving light sampling, without ReSTIR, to improve this in the future.

    In addition, Solari's scene management code is now retained (similar to retained render world optimizations in previous versions of Bevy), and overall much more optimized, leading to significantly reduced CPU costs.

    You may also want to take a look at the new fields in 

    SolariLighting
    . While we aim to set reasonable defaults that will work well across a wide variety of games, there are now many knobs (world cache size, per-pixel light sample count, temporal accumulation, and path tracing bounce count) that can be tweaked to improve performance or quality for your specific scene, project and hardware.

    Improved Compatibility #

    Solari now supports lighting from 

    Atmosphere
    and 
    EnvironmentMapLight
    s on cameras, in addition to the existing support for 
    DirectionalLight
     and emissive meshes. We're hoping to add support for the remaining 
    PointLight
    , 
    SpotLight
    , and 
    RectLight
     types in the near future.

    Solari now also runs on macOS, but note that there is currently no built-in denoiser included in 

    bevy_solari
    for macOS. MetalFX Ray Reconstruction might be a possible solution in the future (contributions welcome!)

    DLSS Updates #

    Finally, our 

    dlss_wgpu
    crate has been updated to support the latest version of DLSS, bringing support for DLSS-RR 4.5, which significantly improves denoising quality in Solari.

    If you were using DLSS in Bevy 0.19, make sure to download and setup the newest version of the DLSS SDK, else you will run into compiler errors.

    BSN Syntax Improvements #

    Authors:@cartPRs:#25318, #25626

    BSN landed with a few idiosyncrasies that caused friction in practice. We made some changes to BSN's syntax this cycle in the interest of improving its ergonomics and clarity. After this, the syntax should largely be nailed down.

    Explicit scene syntax #

    All scene references now require 

    @
    prefixes:
    // Before
bsn! {
    scene_variable
    scene_function()
    @SceneComponent
    {scene_expression}
}

// After
bsn! {
    @scene_variable
    @scene_function()
    @SceneComponent
    @{scene_expression}
}

    In addition to making it easier to spot scene inclusions (and unifying the syntax across cases), this freed us up to make component values much easier to work with!

    No more 
    template_value
    wrappers! #

    You can now remove all of those pesky 

    template_value
    wrappers from your component values:
    // Before
bsn! {
    template_value(component_variable)
    template_value(component_function())
}

// After
bsn! {
    component_variable
    component_function()
}

    Enums "just work" #

    Enums no longer require 

    VariantDefaults
    or 
    FromTemplate
    , provided they implement 
    Default
    and 
    Clone
    :
    // Before
#[derive(Component, Default, Clone, VariantDefaults)]
enum Foo {
    A { x: u32, y: u32 },
    #[default]
    B,
}

bsn! {
    Foo::B
}

// After
#[derive(Component, Default, Clone)]
enum Foo {
    A { x: u32, y: u32 },
    #[default]
    B,
}

bsn! {
    Foo::B
}

    If you were using an enum that didn't support 

    VariantDefaults
    , you can now remove the 
    template_value
    wrapper:
    // Before
bsn! {
    template_value(Foo::A)
}
// After
bsn! {
    Foo::A
}

    The removal of 

    VariantDefaults
    does mean that enums must now have every field specified:
    // Before (y field is initialized to its default value)
bsn! {
    Foo::A { x: 1 }
}

// After (y field must be manually specified)
bsn! {
    Foo::A { x: 1, y: 0 }
}

    We believe this tradeoff is worth it, as it increases BSN's compatibility with arbitrary Rust enums. Rust doesn't support "enum variant defaults" anyway!

    Chained method support #

    The "builder pattern" (and chained methods generally) previously required a 

    template_value
    wrapper. This can now be removed:
    // Before
bsn! {
    template_value(Transform::from_xyz(-2.5, 4.5, 9.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y))
}
// After
bsn! {
    Transform::from_xyz(-2.5, 4.5, 9.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y)
}

    Additionally, you can now remove the 

    template_value
    wrapper in cases like this:
    // Before
bsn! {
    template_value(node.clone())
}
// After
bsn! {
    node.clone()
}

    In general, you should now be able to remove all 

    template_value
    instances from your BSN declarations!

    Improved list syntax #

    BSN previously used commas to separate entities, with optional 

    ()
    around entities to make the boundaries clearer. This resulted in a lot of syntax noise, line noise, and over-indentation:
    bsn! {
    Node 
    Children [
        (
            #OkButton
            @button("Ok")
        ),
        (
            #CancelButton
            @button("Cancel")
        ),
    ]
}

    To avoid this, many developers opted for this syntax instead, which made it very hard to visually distinguish entities:

    bsn! {
    Node 
    Children [
        #OkButton
        @button("Ok"),
        #CancelButton
        @button("Cancel"),
    ]
}

    BSN now uses 

    --
    to separate entities in a list:
    bsn! {
    Node 
    Children [
        #OkButton
        @button("Ok")
        --
        #CancelButton
        @button("Cancel")
    ]
}

    This gives us the best of all worlds: entities are visually distinct, and there is no over-indentation, line noise, or syntax noise (the stats when compared to other competitors in the "markup format" space are very competitive!). Both 

    ()
    and 
    ,
    have been deprecated in this context.

    Using 

    []
    and 
    ()
    for 
    bsn_list!
     (and 
    bsn!
    ) is now discouraged / warned against (ex: 
    bsn_list! []
    ), as it can result in poor rustfmt autoformatting. Instead, use 
    bsn_list! {}
    , which is the only syntax that 
    rustfmt
    won't touch. Don't worry, we plan to build a BSN auto-formatter!
    bsn_list! {
    #Ok @button("Ok")
    --
    #Cancel @button("Cancel")
}

    Ready
    Event #

    Authors:@cartPRs:#25296

    We landed BSN, Bevy's next generation scene system, in our last release. It was missing a key piece though: the ability to easily run logic when a scene is fully "ready" and spawned (ex: all dependencies have loaded, the full hierarchy is present, and all of the initial components are inserted in the scene). This is a critical piece for building cohesive, standalone, composable scenes. It is also necessary to properly layer Bevy logic on top of other scene representations (like glTF).

    The closest we had was the 

    Add
    event for a given component, which runs "top down" (meaning children are not available). We needed a "bottom up" equivalent to enable building logic that relies on the complete loaded and spawned scene.

    The solution is pretty straightforward: trigger a new 

    Ready
    event for each entity in a spawned scene after the full spawn logic has run for that entity (including its descendants).

    This enables the following:

    #[derive(SceneComponent, Default, Clone)]
struct Widget;

impl Widget {
    fn scene() -> impl Scene {
        bsn! {
            Node { width: px(100), height: px(100) }
            on(|ready: On| {
                info!("The full scene, including 'widget.bsn' contents, is available here")
            })
            Children [
                Text("hello")
                --
                :"widget.bsn"
            ]
        }
    }
}

world.spawn(bsn! { @Widget })

    More Feathers Widgets #

    Authors:@viridia, @gagnus, @tmstoreyPRs:#25446, #25079, #24092, #24847, #24784, #24636, #24701

    Feathers, Bevy's opinionated editor-centric UI toolkit, now has more widgets for you to play with:

    Color Input #

    Bevy now has a compact color input selector that displays a color picker widget popup when clicked. This includes a color wheel selector, RGB, and HSL selectors, and a recently used colors grid.

    List View / Scrollbar #

    A scrollable, selectable list view.

    Dropdown Selection #

    A selection field that when clicked, displays a dropdown containing a list of options to select.

    Spawns a menu popup when the menu is opened and despawns it when it is closed. This is in contrast to the normal Menu widget, which just hides the menu.

    Number Input Widget Scrubbing / Dragging #

    The 

    FeathersNumberInput
    widget has been expanded to support both normal text input and scrubbing / dragging. There is a configurable "hard limit" (minimum and maximum value via any input method) and "soft limit" (minimum and maximum value via dragging), in addition to control over floating point precision and step sizes.

    Headless Tab Widgets #

    Authors:@jbuehler23PRs:#25515

    bevy_ui_widgets
    now has headless (bring-your-own-visuals) tab behavior: a 
    TabList
     container and 
    Tab
     headers.

    Selection is managed "externally". 

    SelectedTab
    on the list holds the selected tab; interaction emits 
    ValueChange>
     as a request, applied by the app or by the optional 
    tablist_self_update
     observer.

    Tabs support keyboard shortcuts and integrate with Bevy's focus, interaction, and accessibility systems.

    bsn! {
    TabList
    SelectedTab(Some(first_tab))
    on(tablist_self_update)
    Children [
        Tab Children [ Text("General") ]
        --
        Tab Children [ Text("Rendering") ]
    ]
}

    See the 

    headless_tabs
    example for controlled and self-updating tab lists in both orientations.

    WESL Shaders #

    Authors:@tychedelia, @BenjaminBrienenPRs:#25088

    Bevy's shaders are now written in WESL and the old "Custom Bevy Extended WGSL" language support has been removed.

    WESL is a language standard that extends WGSL to add important usability features like modules, imports, conditional compilation, and more. You can see what that looks like (and render pretty shader toys!) live in your browser in the WESL Playground.

    Bevy has historically handled these things in our own custom WGSL dialect, but we believe it is better for the wider shader ecosystem (and for us) to adopt a common standard where we can pool resources on language improvements, module ecosystems, and IDE tooling. We've been working closely with the WESL team to evolve the standard in a way that fits well into the Bevy picture.

    A critical part of that tooling is language server protocol support, in the form of wgsl-analyzer. That means syntax highlighting, go-to-definition, inlay hints, code folding, formatting and more, once installed for your IDE of choice.

    Custom shaders in the old Bevy WGSL dialect need to be translated to WESL and renamed from 

    .wgsl
    to 
    .wesl
    . Plain WGSL files with no preprocessor directives will keep working.

    Before: Custom Bevy Extended WGSL #

    #import bevy_pbr::forward_io::VertexOutput
#import "shaders/util.wgsl"::hsv_to_rgb
#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
var tint: vec4;
#endif
@group(2) @binding(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) var color: vec4;

    After: WESL #

    import bevy_pbr::render::forward_io::VertexOutput;
import super::util::hsv_to_rgb;
@if(VERTEX_COLORS)
var tint: vec4;
@group(2) @binding(constants::MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP) var color: vec4;

    Mesh Shaders #

    Authors:@ChristopherBiscardiPRs:#25627

    Mesh shaders are now integrated with Bevy's pipeline cache and are available for advanced users to take advantage of. Mesh shaders can be used to render:

  • Meshlets generated using tools like meshoptimizer
  • Procedural grass with dynamic level-of-detail, as seen here
  • Voxels, like nvidium
  • Particles
  • and more

    • Mesh shaders, at a high level, replace the classic vertex shader with a compute shader. This allows generating geometry directly on the GPU and passing those generated primitives directly to the fragment shader without using multiple pipelines or intermediary buffers (to pass data from a compute shader to a render pipeline).

    A 

    MeshPipeline
    contains:
  • an optional task shader (also known as amplification shader)
  • a mesh shader
  • a fragment shader

    • The new 

    MeshPipelineDescriptor
    can be used to define a 
    MeshPipeline
    . That 
    MeshPipeline
     is then used as a 
    RenderPipeline
    , which allows the re-use of Bevy's lower level rendering APIs such as 
    RenderContext::begin_tracked_render_pass
     to take advantage of the new 
    draw_mesh_tasks
     APIs.
    let mut pass = render_context.begin_tracked_render_pass(RenderPassDescriptor {
    label: Some("custom_mesh_shader_pass"),
    color_attachments: &[Some(target.get_color_attachment())],
    depth_stencil_attachment: Some(depth.get_attachment(StoreOp::Store)),
    ..default()
});

pass.set_render_pipeline(mesh_pipeline);
pass.set_bind_group(0, &bind_group, &[view_uniform_offset.offset]);

// draw_mesh_tasks dispatches the task shader if there is one,
// or dispatches the mesh shader if there is no task shader.
pass.draw_mesh_tasks(1, 1, 1);

    It is notable that mesh shaders are an advanced graphics approach with platform-specific performance considerations, and that this is the initial base support for the feature. Higher level user APIs, and easy integration with Bevy's 

    StandardMaterial
    , are left to future work.

    Mesh shaders are not supported on web platforms.

    Check out the new 

    mesh_shader_intro
    example for more usage examples.

    Sprite Materials #

    Authors:@cookie1170PRs:#25415

    Until now, Bevy's sprite renderer has been lacking a major feature: the ability to extend it with custom shaders! With this release, it's now possible to create custom materials for sprites by implementing the 

    MaterialExtension2d
    trait, inserting the 
    SpriteMaterial
     component and adding the 
    SpriteMaterialPlugin
     to your app.

    The shader can use functions exported from 

    bevy_sprite_render::sprite_mesh::functions
    , including:
    // Samples the sprite's final color, including the tint and alpha discard, at a given UV.
fn sample_final_color(uv: vec2, instance_index: u32) -> vec4;

// Samples the sprite's texture without tint and alpha discard at a given UV.
fn sample_sprite_texture(uv: vec2, instance_index: u32) -> vec4;

// Applies tint and alpha discard to the sprite's color.
fn get_final_color(sprite_color: vec4, instance_index: u32) -> vec4;

    Check out the 

    sprite_material
    example to see it in action!

    2D Extended Materials #

    Authors:@cookie1170PRs:#25183

    Bevy now provides a 2D analog to 3D's 

    ExtendedMaterial
    , which can be used to extend an existing material by implementing the 
    MaterialExtension2d
     trait:
    #[derive(AsBindGroup, Reflect, Clone)]
struct MyMaterial {
    #[uniform(20)]
    value: Vec4,
}

impl MaterialExtension2d for MyMaterial {
    fn fragment_shader() -> Option {
        Some("my_material.wesl".into())
    }
}

    This material can now be used in an 

    ExtendedMaterial2d
    struct:
    let handle = materials.add(ExtendedMaterial2d {
    base: ColorMaterial::from_color(Color::WHITE),
    extension: MyMaterial {
        value: Vec4::ZERO,
    },
});
commands.spawn((
    Mesh2d,
    MeshMaterial2d(handle),
));

    Sprite Render Backend Unification #

    Authors:@IceSentryPRs:#25432

    The sprite render backend was replaced by a new backend that reuses a lot of the infrastructure made for 3D. This resulted in improved performance in many cases and also makes future maintenance and improvements easier.

    Pan Orbit Camera #

    Authors:@aevyrie, @taishi-samaPRs:#25434

    We have upstreamed the awesome 

    bevy_editor_cam
    made by @aevyrie as the new 
    PanOrbitCamera
     in our 
    bevy_camera_controller
     crate!

    Usage #

    Add 

    MeshPickingPlugin
    and 
    DefaultPanOrbitCameraPlugins
    :
    app.add_plugins((
    MeshPickingPlugin,
    DefaultPanOrbitCameraPlugins,
))

    Then add the 

    PanOrbitCamera
    component on any 3D camera.
    commands.spawn((
    Camera3d::default(),
    PanOrbitCamera::default(),
))

    Full functionality is shown in the 

    camera/pan_orbit_camera_cad
    example.

    Weak System Ordering with 
    chain_weak
    #

    Authors:@JMS55PRs:#25128

    Ordering large groups of systems with 

    .chain()
    is convenient, but it can be overly strict. If system set 
    X
    is chained before system set 
    Y
    , every system in 
    X
    must finish before any system in 
    Y
    can start, even when the systems involved never touch the same data. This often leaves worker threads idle while they wait for a handful of stragglers at the end of a system set, a pattern that shows up frequently in the render world.

    The new 

    chain_weak()
    , 
    before_weak()
    , and 
    after_weak()
     functions provide a looser alternative. Like their regular counterparts, they request an ordering between successive elements, however that ordering is only kept between systems whose data accesses actually conflict. Systems that don't conflict are left unordered and may run in any order, including in parallel.
    schedule.configure_sets(
    (
        ExtractCommands,
        PrepareMeshes,
        CreateViews,
        Specialize,
        PrepareViews,
        Queue,
        PhaseSort,
        Prepare,
        Render,
        Cleanup,
        PostCleanup,
    )
        .chain_weak(),
);

    When two weakly-ordered systems actually conflict on their data access, a normal ordering is kept between them, so the earlier one still runs first. Two systems that conflict only through a non-conflicting system between them in the chain stay ordered as well. Non-conflicting systems, however, are left free to run in any order and overlap for increased parallelism!

    Two kinds of system are treated as always conflicting, so their ordering is always kept: an earlier system that produces deferred effects such as 

    Commands
    (so the later system observes them, with an 
    ApplyDeferred
     sync point inserted as usual), and exclusive systems (which cannot overlap anything regardless).

    Because the scheduler can only see accesses it tracks, dependencies expressed through interior mutability on read-only accesses, global state, or other untracked methods are not respected. Use 

    chain_weak
    only when your systems don't rely on such hidden ordering, otherwise stick with 
    chain
    .

    Contextual Theming #

    Authors:@viridiaPRs:#24969

    Feathers now supports "contextual theming", meaning that the theme variables can change depending on the parent entity. So widgets that are inside of a dialog box or subpanel can have different colors than widgets that are on a regular panel or window background.

    The design follows that of popular web toolkits like MUI, Radix, or Chakra. There's a new component, 

    ThemeContext
    , which lets you select which color scheme the widget's descendants should use; currently the available schemes are 
    Base
    , 
    Higher
    , 
    Highest
    , and 
    Floating
    , which correspond to the design plans for the Bevy scene editor.

    The theme context is used in conjunction with a new kind of design token, named 

    SemanticToken
    . The lookup process for a color now requires two stages: the 
    ThemeToken
     is converted into a 
    SemanticToken
    , and then the combination of 
    SemanticToken
    and 
    ThemeContext
     is used to look up a color.

    In addition to allowing context-specific color choices, this also makes it easier to design new themes! Instead of having to tediously choose colors for a hundred different theme tokens, the set of semantic tokens is much smaller, and the relationship between token and color is much more intuitive.

    Val::Em
    and 
    Val::Rem
    #

    Authors:@gagnusPRs:#25231

    Bevy UI now supports 

    em
    and 
    rem
     as sizing units. 
    em
    is the current font size (represented by an 
    EmSize
     component), 
    rem
    is a global "root" font size (represented by the existing 
    RemSize
     resource).

    EmSize
    is derived from 
    TextFont
     when one is on the same entity; propagating it down the hierarchy is left to your app.

    This is especially useful if you might want to vary your text size after authoring your UIs, for example as an accessibility feature or just to improve your UI on different devices.

    bsn! {
    Node { width: em(10) }
    Text("Hello")
    TextFont { font_size: FontSize::Rem(1.5) }
}

    The default font-size is now 

    rem(1)
    rather than 
    px(20)
    . This is a no-op if you're not changing 
    RemSize
     but it means your text will scale by default when you do.

    Per-Column Change Ticks #

    Authors:@pcwalton, @SkiFire13PRs:#25157, #25429

    Components can now opt-in to "column summary change ticks":

    #[derive(Component)]
#[component(summary_tick)]
struct MyComponent {
    /* fields here */
}

    When enabled, this will store a "column change tick" in addition to a "per-entity change tick", which allows cheaply skipping the whole column of entities when querying for changes, rather than needing to check every entity's component to see if it has changed.

    This makes mutations more expensive, as they need to write both the column change tick and the entity change tick, but for entities whose changes are queried often, but change infrequently, this tradeoff can easily be worth it! We've seen change ticks result in a 132x speedup in our GPU mesh extraction code!

    FixedNode
    #

    Authors:@ickshonpePRs:#24323

    FixedNode
    is a new marker component for Bevy UI.

    A UI node entity with the 

    FixedNode
    component is positioned relative to the target camera's viewport rather than its parent element. 
    FixedNode
    s don't inherit their parent's layout, clipping or transform context. They behave like a "root node".

    Elliptical Border Radius #

    Authors:@ickshonpePRs:#24779

    Bevy UI can now draw nodes with elliptical border geometry.

    The fields of 

    BorderRadius
    are now 
    CornerRadius
    s to enable different radius to be set for each axis.
    let a = BorderRadius::all(CornerRadius::circular(vh(10.)));
let b = BorderRadius::all(vh(10.)); // a == b
let c = BorderRadius::top_right(CornerRadius::new(px(10.), px(20.)));

    Schedule Randomization #

    Authors:@andriyDevPRs:#25094

    Before a schedule runs (and therefore, your systems), it first computes the system run order based on their ordering constraints (

    .before()
    ,

item.content:encoded:
一句话：ReSTIR 改进让渲染基本无偏，但吃性能多、收益小，于是改成可选并默认关闭，改用 DLSS-RR 撑性能。

要点：

  • Solari（实时路径追踪插件）改进 ReSTIR 后渲染基本无偏、光照更准；移动物体的阴影不再滞后，非金属材质运动时反射不再闪
  • DLSS-RR 变好之后，ReSTIR 在很多场景吃掉可观性能却提升有限，因此改为可选、默认关闭，需要时用 SolariLighting::restir 重新打开
  • 着色器语言转向 WESL（WGSL 的标准化扩展）并成为官方方案；Sprite 可写自定义着色器材质，2D 材质也能像 3D 一样扩展；本版 227 位贡献者、817 个 PR

为什么值得看：「宁可关掉一个先进特性也要换来帧率」是引擎工程的常态判断，这次的公开理由（改进后收益不再抵得上成本）值得作为性能取舍的案例看。

中文摘要：Bevy 0.20 的核心变化在渲染：实时路径追踪插件 Solari 的多个方面都有大幅改进，ReSTIR 实现改善后渲染基本无偏、光照更准确，移动物体的阴影不再滞后，非金属材质在运动中的反射也不再闪烁；在 macOS 上通过 Metal 也能运行。性能方面，由于 DLSS-RR 近期进步明显，而 ReSTIR 在不少场景中占用可观性能却对画质提升有限，团队把它改为可选并默认关闭，若仍需要可显式开启 SolariLighting::restir。此外 Bevy 正式采用 WESL 作为着色器语言，Sprite 支持自定义着色器材质、2D 材质可像 3D 一样扩展，Feathers UI 增加多个控件，版本由 227 位贡献者的 817 个 PR 组成。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：Bevy（中文）

原文发布：2026-10-08

本期推送：2026-10-24

Bevy 0.20

Posted on October 8, 2026 by Bevy Contributors

The Zorah scene rendered in Bevy Solari

Thanks to 227 contributors, 817 pull requests, community reviewers, and our generous donors, we're happy to announce the Bevy 0.20 release on crates.io!

For those who don't know, Bevy is a refreshingly simple data-driven game engine built in Rust. You can check out our Quick Start Guide to try it today. It's free and open source forever! You can grab the full source code on GitHub. Check out Bevy Assets for a collection of community-developed plugins, games, and learning resources.

To update an existing Bevy App or Plugin to Bevy 0.20, check out our 0.19 to 0.20 Migration Guide.

Since our last release a few months ago we've added a ton of new features, bug fixes, and quality of life tweaks, but here are some of the highlights:

  • Solari and DLSS: Solari, Bevy's realtime pathtraced renderer, is now faster, more accurate, supports more Bevy rendering features, and runs on macOS via Metal!
  • BSN Syntax Improvements: BSN, Bevy's new scene system, had some syntax changes that made it much easier to read and compose
  • Ready Event: BSN scene entities now trigger an observable 
    Ready
     event when all of their children have been spawned.
  • More UI Widgets: Bevy Feathers, Bevy's opinionated editor-centric UI toolkit, now has Color Input, Scrollable List View, Dropdown Selection, and Lazy Menu widgets. The Number Input widget is now scrubbable / draggable, and we've added Headless Tab Widgets.
  • WESL Shaders: Bevy has officially adopted the WESL shader language (a standardized extension of WGSL). WESL is already an improvement over Bevy's old custom WGSL dialect, and we've been working with the WESL team to plan out the future of shader development in Bevy.
  • Sprite Materials and Extended 2D Materials: It is now possible to create custom shader materials for Sprites, and 2D mesh materials can now be extended like they can in 3D.
  • Pan Orbit Camera: Bevy now has a "pan orbit camera", making it possible to navigate scenes in a CAD-like way.

    • Solari and DLSS #

    Authors:@JMS55, @mate-h, @stuartparmenterPRs:#24667, #24767, #25082, #25123, #25244, #25423, #25513, #25518, #25703, #25704, #25787, #25814

    Solari, Bevy's realtime pathtraced renderer, has seen major improvements to pretty much every aspect of the plugin!

    Read JMS55's blog for the technical details, or continue reading below for the high level overview.

    Improved Image Quality #

    Thanks to improvements in our ReSTIR implementation, rendering is now mostly unbiased, leading to much more accurate lighting.

    Additionally, thanks to some other changes, moving objects no longer have shadows that lag behind, and reflections now look significantly less shimmery in motion, especially for non-metallic materials.

    Improved Performance #

    DLSS-RR has gotten very good in recent updates, and for many scenes, ReSTIR costs a decent chunk of performance, and does not significantly improve image quality.

    As a result, we've decided to make ReSTIR optional, and turn it off by default.

    If you were using Solari in Bevy 0.19, check if the loss of ReSTIR affects your scene, and if so re-enable 

    SolariLighting::restir
    .

    With ReSTIR off, expect reduced shadow quality and missing shadows in motion in scenes with many lights. We are exploring cheaper ways of improving light sampling, without ReSTIR, to improve this in the future.

    In addition, Solari's scene management code is now retained (similar to retained render world optimizations in previous versions of Bevy), and overall much more optimized, leading to significantly reduced CPU costs.

    You may also want to take a look at the new fields in 

    SolariLighting
    . While we aim to set reasonable defaults that will work well across a wide variety of games, there are now many knobs (world cache size, per-pixel light sample count, temporal accumulation, and path tracing bounce count) that can be tweaked to improve performance or quality for your specific scene, project and hardware.

    Improved Compatibility #

    Solari now supports lighting from 

    Atmosphere
    and 
    EnvironmentMapLight
    s on cameras, in addition to the existing support for 
    DirectionalLight
     and emissive meshes. We're hoping to add support for the remaining 
    PointLight
    , 
    SpotLight
    , and 
    RectLight
     types in the near future.

    Solari now also runs on macOS, but note that there is currently no built-in denoiser included in 

    bevy_solari
    for macOS. MetalFX Ray Reconstruction might be a possible solution in the future (contributions welcome!)

    DLSS Updates #

    Finally, our 

    dlss_wgpu
    crate has been updated to support the latest version of DLSS, bringing support for DLSS-RR 4.5, which significantly improves denoising quality in Solari.

    If you were using DLSS in Bevy 0.19, make sure to download and setup the newest version of the DLSS SDK, else you will run into compiler errors.

    BSN Syntax Improvements #

    Authors:@cartPRs:#25318, #25626

    BSN landed with a few idiosyncrasies that caused friction in practice. We made some changes to BSN's syntax this cycle in the interest of improving its ergonomics and clarity. After this, the syntax should largely be nailed down.

    Explicit scene syntax #

    All scene references now require 

    @
    prefixes:
    // Before
bsn! {
    scene_variable
    scene_function()
    @SceneComponent
    {scene_expression}
}

// After
bsn! {
    @scene_variable
    @scene_function()
    @SceneComponent
    @{scene_expression}
}

    In addition to making it easier to spot scene inclusions (and unifying the syntax across cases), this freed us up to make component values much easier to work with!

    No more 
    template_value
    wrappers! #

    You can now remove all of those pesky 

    template_value
    wrappers from your component values:
    // Before
bsn! {
    template_value(component_variable)
    template_value(component_function())
}

// After
bsn! {
    component_variable
    component_function()
}

    Enums "just work" #

    Enums no longer require 

    VariantDefaults
    or 
    FromTemplate
    , provided they implement 
    Default
    and 
    Clone
    :
    // Before
#[derive(Component, Default, Clone, VariantDefaults)]
enum Foo {
    A { x: u32, y: u32 },
    #[default]
    B,
}

bsn! {
    Foo::B
}

// After
#[derive(Component, Default, Clone)]
enum Foo {
    A { x: u32, y: u32 },
    #[default]
    B,
}

bsn! {
    Foo::B
}

    If you were using an enum that didn't support 

    VariantDefaults
    , you can now remove the 
    template_value
    wrapper:
    // Before
bsn! {
    template_value(Foo::A)
}
// After
bsn! {
    Foo::A
}

    The removal of 

    VariantDefaults
    does mean that enums must now have every field specified:
    // Before (y field is initialized to its default value)
bsn! {
    Foo::A { x: 1 }
}

// After (y field must be manually specified)
bsn! {
    Foo::A { x: 1, y: 0 }
}

    We believe this tradeoff is worth it, as it increases BSN's compatibility with arbitrary Rust enums. Rust doesn't support "enum variant defaults" anyway!

    Chained method support #

    The "builder pattern" (and chained methods generally) previously required a 

    template_value
    wrapper. This can now be removed:
    // Before
bsn! {
    template_value(Transform::from_xyz(-2.5, 4.5, 9.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y))
}
// After
bsn! {
    Transform::from_xyz(-2.5, 4.5, 9.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y)
}

    Additionally, you can now remove the 

    template_value
    wrapper in cases like this:
    // Before
bsn! {
    template_value(node.clone())
}
// After
bsn! {
    node.clone()
}

    In general, you should now be able to remove all 

    template_value
    instances from your BSN declarations!

    Improved list syntax #

    BSN previously used commas to separate entities, with optional 

    ()
    around entities to make the boundaries clearer. This resulted in a lot of syntax noise, line noise, and over-indentation:
    bsn! {
    Node 
    Children [
        (
            #OkButton
            @button("Ok")
        ),
        (
            #CancelButton
            @button("Cancel")
        ),
    ]
}

    To avoid this, many developers opted for this syntax instead, which made it very hard to visually distinguish entities:

    bsn! {
    Node 
    Children [
        #OkButton
        @button("Ok"),
        #CancelButton
        @button("Cancel"),
    ]
}

    BSN now uses 

    --
    to separate entities in a list:
    bsn! {
    Node 
    Children [
        #OkButton
        @button("Ok")
        --
        #CancelButton
        @button("Cancel")
    ]
}

    This gives us the best of all worlds: entities are visually distinct, and there is no over-indentation, line noise, or syntax noise (the stats when compared to other competitors in the "markup format" space are very competitive!). Both 

    ()
    and 
    ,
    have been deprecated in this context.

    Using 

    []
    and 
    ()
    for 
    bsn_list!
     (and 
    bsn!
    ) is now discouraged / warned against (ex: 
    bsn_list! []
    ), as it can result in poor rustfmt autoformatting. Instead, use 
    bsn_list! {}
    , which is the only syntax that 
    rustfmt
    won't touch. Don't worry, we plan to build a BSN auto-formatter!
    bsn_list! {
    #Ok @button("Ok")
    --
    #Cancel @button("Cancel")
}

    Ready
    Event #

    Authors:@cartPRs:#25296

    We landed BSN, Bevy's next generation scene system, in our last release. It was missing a key piece though: the ability to easily run logic when a scene is fully "ready" and spawned (ex: all dependencies have loaded, the full hierarchy is present, and all of the initial components are inserted in the scene). This is a critical piece for building cohesive, standalone, composable scenes. It is also necessary to properly layer Bevy logic on top of other scene representations (like glTF).

    The closest we had was the 

    Add
    event for a given component, which runs "top down" (meaning children are not available). We needed a "bottom up" equivalent to enable building logic that relies on the complete loaded and spawned scene.

    The solution is pretty straightforward: trigger a new 

    Ready
    event for each entity in a spawned scene after the full spawn logic has run for that entity (including its descendants).

    This enables the following:

    #[derive(SceneComponent, Default, Clone)]
struct Widget;

impl Widget {
    fn scene() -> impl Scene {
        bsn! {
            Node { width: px(100), height: px(100) }
            on(|ready: On| {
                info!("The full scene, including 'widget.bsn' contents, is available here")
            })
            Children [
                Text("hello")
                --
                :"widget.bsn"
            ]
        }
    }
}

world.spawn(bsn! { @Widget })

    More Feathers Widgets #

    Authors:@viridia, @gagnus, @tmstoreyPRs:#25446, #25079, #24092, #24847, #24784, #24636, #24701

    Feathers, Bevy's opinionated editor-centric UI toolkit, now has more widgets for you to play with:

    Color Input #

    Bevy now has a compact color input selector that displays a color picker widget popup when clicked. This includes a color wheel selector, RGB, and HSL selectors, and a recently used colors grid.

    List View / Scrollbar #

    A scrollable, selectable list view.

    Dropdown Selection #

    A selection field that when clicked, displays a dropdown containing a list of options to select.

    Spawns a menu popup when the menu is opened and despawns it when it is closed. This is in contrast to the normal Menu widget, which just hides the menu.

    Number Input Widget Scrubbing / Dragging #

    The 

    FeathersNumberInput
    widget has been expanded to support both normal text input and scrubbing / dragging. There is a configurable "hard limit" (minimum and maximum value via any input method) and "soft limit" (minimum and maximum value via dragging), in addition to control over floating point precision and step sizes.

    Headless Tab Widgets #

    Authors:@jbuehler23PRs:#25515

    bevy_ui_widgets
    now has headless (bring-your-own-visuals) tab behavior: a 
    TabList
     container and 
    Tab
     headers.

    Selection is managed "externally". 

    SelectedTab
    on the list holds the selected tab; interaction emits 
    ValueChange>
     as a request, applied by the app or by the optional 
    tablist_self_update
     observer.

    Tabs support keyboard shortcuts and integrate with Bevy's focus, interaction, and accessibility systems.

    bsn! {
    TabList
    SelectedTab(Some(first_tab))
    on(tablist_self_update)
    Children [
        Tab Children [ Text("General") ]
        --
        Tab Children [ Text("Rendering") ]
    ]
}

    See the 

    headless_tabs
    example for controlled and self-updating tab lists in both orientations.

    WESL Shaders #

    Authors:@tychedelia, @BenjaminBrienenPRs:#25088

    Bevy's shaders are now written in WESL and the old "Custom Bevy Extended WGSL" language support has been removed.

    WESL is a language standard that extends WGSL to add important usability features like modules, imports, conditional compilation, and more. You can see what that looks like (and render pretty shader toys!) live in your browser in the WESL Playground.

    Bevy has historically handled these things in our own custom WGSL dialect, but we believe it is better for the wider shader ecosystem (and for us) to adopt a common standard where we can pool resources on language improvements, module ecosystems, and IDE tooling. We've been working closely with the WESL team to evolve the standard in a way that fits well into the Bevy picture.

    A critical part of that tooling is language server protocol support, in the form of wgsl-analyzer. That means syntax highlighting, go-to-definition, inlay hints, code folding, formatting and more, once installed for your IDE of choice.

    Custom shaders in the old Bevy WGSL dialect need to be translated to WESL and renamed from 

    .wgsl
    to 
    .wesl
    . Plain WGSL files with no preprocessor directives will keep working.

    Before: Custom Bevy Extended WGSL #

    #import bevy_pbr::forward_io::VertexOutput
#import "shaders/util.wgsl"::hsv_to_rgb
#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
var tint: vec4;
#endif
@group(2) @binding(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) var color: vec4;

    After: WESL #

    import bevy_pbr::render::forward_io::VertexOutput;
import super::util::hsv_to_rgb;
@if(VERTEX_COLORS)
var tint: vec4;
@group(2) @binding(constants::MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP) var color: vec4;

    Mesh Shaders #

    Authors:@ChristopherBiscardiPRs:#25627

    Mesh shaders are now integrated with Bevy's pipeline cache and are available for advanced users to take advantage of. Mesh shaders can be used to render:

  • Meshlets generated using tools like meshoptimizer
  • Procedural grass with dynamic level-of-detail, as seen here
  • Voxels, like nvidium
  • Particles
  • and more

    • Mesh shaders, at a high level, replace the classic vertex shader with a compute shader. This allows generating geometry directly on the GPU and passing those generated primitives directly to the fragment shader without using multiple pipelines or intermediary buffers (to pass data from a compute shader to a render pipeline).

    A 

    MeshPipeline
    contains:
  • an optional task shader (also known as amplification shader)
  • a mesh shader
  • a fragment shader

    • The new 

    MeshPipelineDescriptor
    can be used to define a 
    MeshPipeline
    . That 
    MeshPipeline
     is then used as a 
    RenderPipeline
    , which allows the re-use of Bevy's lower level rendering APIs such as 
    RenderContext::begin_tracked_render_pass
     to take advantage of the new 
    draw_mesh_tasks
     APIs.
    let mut pass = render_context.begin_tracked_render_pass(RenderPassDescriptor {
    label: Some("custom_mesh_shader_pass"),
    color_attachments: &[Some(target.get_color_attachment())],
    depth_stencil_attachment: Some(depth.get_attachment(StoreOp::Store)),
    ..default()
});

pass.set_render_pipeline(mesh_pipeline);
pass.set_bind_group(0, &bind_group, &[view_uniform_offset.offset]);

// draw_mesh_tasks dispatches the task shader if there is one,
// or dispatches the mesh shader if there is no task shader.
pass.draw_mesh_tasks(1, 1, 1);

    It is notable that mesh shaders are an advanced graphics approach with platform-specific performance considerations, and that this is the initial base support for the feature. Higher level user APIs, and easy integration with Bevy's 

    StandardMaterial
    , are left to future work.

    Mesh shaders are not supported on web platforms.

    Check out the new 

    mesh_shader_intro
    example for more usage examples.

    Sprite Materials #

    Authors:@cookie1170PRs:#25415

    Until now, Bevy's sprite renderer has been lacking a major feature: the ability to extend it with custom shaders! With this release, it's now possible to create custom materials for sprites by implementing the 

    MaterialExtension2d
    trait, inserting the 
    SpriteMaterial
     component and adding the 
    SpriteMaterialPlugin
     to your app.

    The shader can use functions exported from 

    bevy_sprite_render::sprite_mesh::functions
    , including:
    // Samples the sprite's final color, including the tint and alpha discard, at a given UV.
fn sample_final_color(uv: vec2, instance_index: u32) -> vec4;

// Samples the sprite's texture without tint and alpha discard at a given UV.
fn sample_sprite_texture(uv: vec2, instance_index: u32) -> vec4;

// Applies tint and alpha discard to the sprite's color.
fn get_final_color(sprite_color: vec4, instance_index: u32) -> vec4;

    Check out the 

    sprite_material
    example to see it in action!

    2D Extended Materials #

    Authors:@cookie1170PRs:#25183

    Bevy now provides a 2D analog to 3D's 

    ExtendedMaterial
    , which can be used to extend an existing material by implementing the 
    MaterialExtension2d
     trait:
    #[derive(AsBindGroup, Reflect, Clone)]
struct MyMaterial {
    #[uniform(20)]
    value: Vec4,
}

impl MaterialExtension2d for MyMaterial {
    fn fragment_shader() -> Option {
        Some("my_material.wesl".into())
    }
}

    This material can now be used in an 

    ExtendedMaterial2d
    struct:
    let handle = materials.add(ExtendedMaterial2d {
    base: ColorMaterial::from_color(Color::WHITE),
    extension: MyMaterial {
        value: Vec4::ZERO,
    },
});
commands.spawn((
    Mesh2d,
    MeshMaterial2d(handle),
));

    Sprite Render Backend Unification #

    Authors:@IceSentryPRs:#25432

    The sprite render backend was replaced by a new backend that reuses a lot of the infrastructure made for 3D. This resulted in improved performance in many cases and also makes future maintenance and improvements easier.

    Pan Orbit Camera #

    Authors:@aevyrie, @taishi-samaPRs:#25434

    We have upstreamed the awesome 

    bevy_editor_cam
    made by @aevyrie as the new 
    PanOrbitCamera
     in our 
    bevy_camera_controller
     crate!

    Usage #

    Add 

    MeshPickingPlugin
    and 
    DefaultPanOrbitCameraPlugins
    :
    app.add_plugins((
    MeshPickingPlugin,
    DefaultPanOrbitCameraPlugins,
))

    Then add the 

    PanOrbitCamera
    component on any 3D camera.
    commands.spawn((
    Camera3d::default(),
    PanOrbitCamera::default(),
))

    Full functionality is shown in the 

    camera/pan_orbit_camera_cad
    example.

    Weak System Ordering with 
    chain_weak
    #

    Authors:@JMS55PRs:#25128

    Ordering large groups of systems with 

    .chain()
    is convenient, but it can be overly strict. If system set 
    X
    is chained before system set 
    Y
    , every system in 
    X
    must finish before any system in 
    Y
    can start, even when the systems involved never touch the same data. This often leaves worker threads idle while they wait for a handful of stragglers at the end of a system set, a pattern that shows up frequently in the render world.

    The new 

    chain_weak()
    , 
    before_weak()
    , and 
    after_weak()
     functions provide a looser alternative. Like their regular counterparts, they request an ordering between successive elements, however that ordering is only kept between systems whose data accesses actually conflict. Systems that don't conflict are left unordered and may run in any order, including in parallel.
    schedule.configure_sets(
    (
        ExtractCommands,
        PrepareMeshes,
        CreateViews,
        Specialize,
        PrepareViews,
        Queue,
        PhaseSort,
        Prepare,
        Render,
        Cleanup,
        PostCleanup,
    )
        .chain_weak(),
);

    When two weakly-ordered systems actually conflict on their data access, a normal ordering is kept between them, so the earlier one still runs first. Two systems that conflict only through a non-conflicting system between them in the chain stay ordered as well. Non-conflicting systems, however, are left free to run in any order and overlap for increased parallelism!

    Two kinds of system are treated as always conflicting, so their ordering is always kept: an earlier system that produces deferred effects such as 

    Commands
    (so the later system observes them, with an 
    ApplyDeferred
     sync point inserted as usual), and exclusive systems (which cannot overlap anything regardless).

    Because the scheduler can only see accesses it tracks, dependencies expressed through interior mutability on read-only accesses, global state, or other untracked methods are not respected. Use 

    chain_weak
    only when your systems don't rely on such hidden ordering, otherwise stick with 
    chain
    .

    Contextual Theming #

    Authors:@viridiaPRs:#24969

    Feathers now supports "contextual theming", meaning that the theme variables can change depending on the parent entity. So widgets that are inside of a dialog box or subpanel can have different colors than widgets that are on a regular panel or window background.

    The design follows that of popular web toolkits like MUI, Radix, or Chakra. There's a new component, 

    ThemeContext
    , which lets you select which color scheme the widget's descendants should use; currently the available schemes are 
    Base
    , 
    Higher
    , 
    Highest
    , and 
    Floating
    , which correspond to the design plans for the Bevy scene editor.

    The theme context is used in conjunction with a new kind of design token, named 

    SemanticToken
    . The lookup process for a color now requires two stages: the 
    ThemeToken
     is converted into a 
    SemanticToken
    , and then the combination of 
    SemanticToken
    and 
    ThemeContext
     is used to look up a color.

    In addition to allowing context-specific color choices, this also makes it easier to design new themes! Instead of having to tediously choose colors for a hundred different theme tokens, the set of semantic tokens is much smaller, and the relationship between token and color is much more intuitive.

    Val::Em
    and 
    Val::Rem
    #

    Authors:@gagnusPRs:#25231

    Bevy UI now supports 

    em
    and 
    rem
     as sizing units. 
    em
    is the current font size (represented by an 
    EmSize
     component), 
    rem
    is a global "root" font size (represented by the existing 
    RemSize
     resource).

    EmSize
    is derived from 
    TextFont
     when one is on the same entity; propagating it down the hierarchy is left to your app.

    This is especially useful if you might want to vary your text size after authoring your UIs, for example as an accessibility feature or just to improve your UI on different devices.

    bsn! {
    Node { width: em(10) }
    Text("Hello")
    TextFont { font_size: FontSize::Rem(1.5) }
}

    The default font-size is now 

    rem(1)
    rather than 
    px(20)
    . This is a no-op if you're not changing 
    RemSize
     but it means your text will scale by default when you do.

    Per-Column Change Ticks #

    Authors:@pcwalton, @SkiFire13PRs:#25157, #25429

    Components can now opt-in to "column summary change ticks":

    #[derive(Component)]
#[component(summary_tick)]
struct MyComponent {
    /* fields here */
}

    When enabled, this will store a "column change tick" in addition to a "per-entity change tick", which allows cheaply skipping the whole column of entities when querying for changes, rather than needing to check every entity's component to see if it has changed.

    This makes mutations more expensive, as they need to write both the column change tick and the entity change tick, but for entities whose changes are queried often, but change infrequently, this tradeoff can easily be worth it! We've seen change ticks result in a 132x speedup in our GPU mesh extraction code!

    FixedNode
    #

    Authors:@ickshonpePRs:#24323

    FixedNode
    is a new marker component for Bevy UI.

    A UI node entity with the 

    FixedNode
    component is positioned relative to the target camera's viewport rather than its parent element. 
    FixedNode
    s don't inherit their parent's layout, clipping or transform context. They behave like a "root node".

    Elliptical Border Radius #

    Authors:@ickshonpePRs:#24779

    Bevy UI can now draw nodes with elliptical border geometry.

    The fields of 

    BorderRadius
    are now 
    CornerRadius
    s to enable different radius to be set for each axis.

let b = BorderRadius::all(vh(10.)); // a == b

item.title: 软阴影别给所有像素用同一组采样偏移：从白噪声到时空蓝噪声的抖动选型 ｜ 阴影采样抖动算法全解析：从白噪声到时空蓝噪声
item.category: 公众号·游戏AI编程与图形渲染
item.description:
一句话：抖动不是为了好看，而是把低频条纹换成能被 TAA 与时域累积抹掉的高频噪声——选错抖动，降噪器也救不回来。

要点：

  • 问题不是噪声而是 banding：PCF/PCSS 只有 16–32 次采样去逼近连续积分，所有像素共用同一组偏移时，相邻像素遮挡值完全相同，形成肉眼可见的条纹
  • 先分清两个正交概念：采样核形状（所有像素共用，均匀网格 / 均匀圆盘 / 泊松盘…）与逐像素抖动序列，混为一谈是最常见的设计错误
  • 抖动序列从白噪声一路讲到时空蓝噪声，给出原理、公式与可直接抄的代码，最后附对比表与实战选型建议

为什么值得看：软阴影的质量上限往往由抖动序列决定，而它又是最容易被随手糊一个 rand() 的地方。PCF/PCSS 实现要复现或调优时，可以直接按这篇的对比表选序列，而不是凭感觉试。

中文摘要：做软阴影（PCF / PCSS）或任何有限次采样的效果时都会遇到同一个问题：采样点不够用。16–32 次采样去逼近连续积分，若所有像素共用同一组采样偏移，结果不是噪声而是一条条肉眼可见的带状条纹，因为同一光源下相邻像素算出的遮挡值完全相同。解决思路很统一：给每个像素施加不同的抖动，把规则的 banding 打散成高频噪声——高频噪声对人眼更友好，而且能被 TAA、时域累积或降噪器抹掉，条纹则不能。文章先区分两个常被混淆的正交概念：采样核形状与逐像素抖动序列，再系统梳理从白噪声到蓝噪声、时空蓝噪声的抖动算法，给出原理、公式与可直接使用的代码，最后给出对比表和按场景的选型建议。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：公众号·游戏AI编程与图形渲染（中文）

原文发布：2026-10-15

本期推送：2026-10-24

做软阴影（PCF / PCSS）或者任何有限次采样的效果时，都会遇到同一个问题：采样点不够用。

比如 PCSS 里你只能用 16~32 次采样去逼近一个连续积分，如果所有像素都用同一组采样偏移，结果不是噪声，而是一条一条肉眼可见的带状条纹（banding）——因为同一个光源下相邻像素算出来的遮挡值完全相同。

解决思路非常统一：给每个像素施加一个不同的抖动（dither），把空间上规则的 banding 打散成高频噪声。噪声虽然难看，但它有两个好处：

  • 高频噪声对人眼远比低频条纹「友好」；
  • 噪声可以被 TAA / 时域累积 / 降噪器轻松抹掉，而条纹不能。

    • 下面这张图就是全文的直觉起点——同一条连续的半影梯度，欠采样后变成刺眼的条纹，而抖动把条纹换成了人眼更能容忍、且可被时域滤波抹掉的噪声：

    这篇文章把阴影采样里常用的抖动算法系统梳理一遍，给出原理、公式和可直接抄的代码，最后给一张对比表和实战选型建议。

    先用一张流程图把整条采样链路串起来，后面每一节都对应图里的一个方块：

    一、先分清两个正交的概念

    很多人会把「泊松盘采样」和「蓝噪声抖动」混为一谈，其实它们作用在完全不同的环节。一个带抖动的阴影采样器，由两部分组成：

    ① 采样核的形状（所有像素共用）：n 个 tap 在圆盘/平面上怎么摆。

  • 均匀网格：最差，方向性明显；
  • 均匀圆盘（极坐标均匀）：一般；
  • 泊松盘（Poisson Disk）：任意两点距离有下限，覆盖均匀无聚集，是软阴影采样核的事实标准。

    • ② 逐像素的去相关源（每像素不同）：怎么让相邻像素用「同一核的不同旋转/不同排列」。

  • 哈希白噪声、Wang Hash；
  • IGN（Interleaved Gradient Noise）；
  • Bayer 有序抖动 / 棋盘格；
  • 蓝噪声纹理（BNDS）、STBN；
  • 黄金比率 / 低差异序列（时域）。

    • 常见组合是：泊松盘定 taps 位置 + 每像素一个随机角度 θ，把整盘 taps 旋转 θ：

    所以下面讲算法时请注意它属于哪一层：泊松盘是第①层，其余全是第②层。用一张图把两层的分工固定下来：

    二、采样核层：泊松盘采样（Poisson Disk）

    2.1 为什么用它当采样核

    软阴影本质是圆盘（或球面）上的积分，tap 之间如果距离太近就是浪费——它们采到的信息高度相关。泊松盘约束任意两点最小距离 ≥ r，让有限 taps 的覆盖最均匀。下图左边是均匀网格（明显的横竖方向性 + 圆盘边缘浪费），右边是泊松盘（点距均匀、无聚集）：

    经典生成算法：

  • Dart Throwing：随机撒点，违反最小距离就丢弃，简单但慢；
  • Best-Candidate：每轮生成 k 个候选，保留离现有点集最远的那个，质量接近 dart throwing，快得多；
  • Bridson 算法（2007）：用背景网格加速，线性时间，是离线生成的常用选择。

    • 实际项目里不需要运行时生成——离线生成一次，硬编码成常量数组：

    // 16 tap 泊松盘（示意，实际数值由离线 best-candidate 生成）const vec2 poissonDisk[16] = vec2[](    vec2(-0.9420, -0.3993), vec2( 0.9455,  0.7689),    vec2(-0.0941, -0.9293), vec2( 0.3449,  0.2938),    vec2(-0.9158,  0.4577), vec2(-0.8154, -0.8791),    vec2(-0.3827,  0.2767), vec2( 0.9748,  0.7564),    vec2( 0.4432, -0.9751), vec2( 0.5374, -0.4737),    vec2(-0.2649, -0.4184), vec2( 0.7919,  0.1909),    vec2(-0.2418,  0.9970), vec2(-0.1998, -0.0733),    vec2( 0.1715, -0.4562), vec2(-0.2911,  0.6493));

    2.2 配合逐像素旋转去 banding

    float ShadowPCF(sampler2DShadow shadowMap, vec3 shadowCoord, float radius, float theta){    float s = sin(theta), c = cos(theta);    mat2 rot = mat2(c, -s, s, c);    float sum = 0.0;    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {        vec2 offset = rot * poissonDisk[i] * radius;        sum += texture(shadowMap, vec3(shadowCoord.xy + offset, shadowCoord.z));    }    return sum / 16.0;}

    θ 从哪里来？这正是第②层各算法的分工。

    三、逐像素抖动层：六种主流方案

    3.1 白噪声与哈希：最朴素的起点

    fract-sin 哈希（GPU 上最常用的伪随机）：

    float rand(vec2 p) {    return fract(sin(dot(p, vec2(12.9898, 78.233))) * 43758.5453);}float theta = rand(gl_FragCoord.xy) * 6.2831853;

    Wang Hash（整数域，质量好于 fract-sin，无精度问题）：

    uint wang_hash(uint seed){    seed = (seed ^ 61u) ^ (seed >> 16u);    seed *= 9u;    seed = seed ^ (seed >> 4u);    seed *= 0x27d4eb2du;    seed = seed ^ (seed >> 15u);    return seed;}// 用法：theta = float(wang_hash(uint(gl_FragCoord.x) * 1973u//            ^ uint(gl_FragCoord.y) * 9277u)) * (1.0/4294967296.0) * 6.2831853;

    问题：白噪声的频谱是全频段平坦的，包含大量低频能量。低频噪声 = 大块的明暗斑块，时域滤波很难收敛干净，视觉上就是「擦不掉的脏」。这正是后面所有算法要解决的问题。

    下面这张对比图是理解整篇文章的关键。上排是白噪声，右侧频谱图中心（低频区）能量很强；下排是蓝噪声，空间上看更「均匀细碎」，频谱中心是一个明显的空洞——低频能量被彻底抽走，只留高频。人眼对低频最敏感，所以蓝噪声「看起来」误差最小：

    一个常见误区：Wang Hash 只是「更好的白噪声生成器」，它并不改善噪声的频谱形状。要改善频谱，得换空间分布结构。

    3.2 Interleaved Gradient Noise（IGN）

    来自 Jorge Jimenez（Activision）的 Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty（SIGGRAPH 2014）。核心观察：有规律的、梯度交错的小结构噪声，比白噪声更容易被 TAA 吸收。

    公式极其简洁：

    float ign(vec2 pixel){    return fract(52.9829189 * fract(0.06711056 * pixel.x                                  + 0.00583715 * pixel.y));}float theta = ign(gl_FragCoord.xy) * 6.2831853;

    特点：

  • 零纹理、零状态、一个 MAD 指令级别，几乎是免费的；
  • 空间上是规则的梯度交错图案，低频能量比白噪声少；
  • 和 TAA 配合极佳（CoD 的 SSR、体积雾都靠它）；
  • 单帧静态看会有轻微规则纹理感，动起来或累积后消失。

    • 3.3 Bayer 有序抖动与棋盘格

    Bayer 矩阵是最经典的有序抖动，4x4 版本（值除以 16 归一化）：

    特点是「最大化已点亮像素之间的距离」，频谱上能量被推到高频，类似粗糙版的蓝噪声。优点是完全确定、可平铺；缺点是规则图案在静态画面上能被看出来（复古抖动风格）。

    棋盘格（checkerboard）是 2x2 Bayer 的特例，但它的用法不太一样——不是拿来生成 θ，而是拿来砍采样量：

  • 棋盘格的一种颜色采「样本集合 A」，另一种颜色采「样本集合 B」，每像素成本减半；
  • 帧奇偶时间翻转：偶数帧像素 (x+y) 为偶时采 A，奇数帧翻转采 B。两帧合起来每个像素都覆盖过 A 和 B，TAA 一累积就是全量采样：
    • bool parity = ((int(gl_FragCoord.x) + int(gl_FragCoord.y) + frameIndex) & 1) == 0;vec2 offset = rot * (parity ? tapsA[i] : tapsB[i]);

    这是「空间欠采样 + 时间补偿」的思路，在半分辨率阴影、半分辨率 AO 里非常常见。前提是你的 TAA 足够稳，否则翻转帧之间会闪。

    3.4 蓝噪声纹理（Blue Noise / BNDS）

    蓝噪声的定义是频谱上只有高频能量、低频区为空的噪声。人眼对低频敏感、对高频迟钝，所以同样的采样误差，按蓝噪声分布「看起来」最少。

    与 Bayer 的区别：Bayer 是规则周期图案，蓝噪声是无规则但满足最小距离约束的分布——可以把它理解成「抖动的泊松盘」。

  • 离线用 Void-and-Cluster（Ulichney 1993）算法生成，并做边缘回绕使其可无缝平铺；
  • 运行时一次纹理 fetch，按屏幕坐标取模寻址：
    • float theta = texelFetch(blueNoiseTex,    ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) % textureSize(blueNoiseTex, 0), 0).r * 6.2831853;
  • 工程界有现成的免费高质量蓝噪声纹理（如 Christoph Peters 的 Moments in Graphics 博客提供的 STBN/BNDS 资源），Unity HDRP、Unreal 引擎内部也都是直接内置蓝噪声纹理。

    • 定位：第②层的「单帧质量天花板」，代价是一张纹理。没有时域累积的纯前向渲染里，蓝噪声通常是最佳选择。

    3.5 时空蓝噪声（STBN）

    蓝噪声只优化了空间维。如果渲染是逐帧变化 + 时域累积的，理想情况是：每一帧在空间上是蓝噪声，同一像素在时间维也去相关。

    这里要澄清一个常见的出处混淆。业界有两条相关但不同的路线：

  • Heitz & Belcour, SIGGRAPH 2019（A Low-Discrepancy Sampler that Distributes Monte Carlo Errors as a Blue Noise in Screen Space）：思路是逐像素重排采样序列，让蒙特卡洛误差在屏幕空间上呈蓝噪声分布，本质是「样本置换 + 空间蓝噪声掩码」，并不是一张 3D 纹理。
  • Wolfe et al. (NVIDIA), EGSR 2022（Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks，即通常说的 STBN 纹理）：把蓝噪声掩码直接做成 3D 纹理，xy 是屏幕空间，z 是帧序号——下面代码里 
    stbnTex
     用的就是这套。

    • 以 3D 纹理版 STBN 为例，它的两个核心性质是：

  • 每个 z 切片单独看都是一张合法的空间蓝噪声；
  • 沿 z 轴（时间维）看，同一像素在相邻帧的取值也满足蓝噪声关系，误差互相「错开」，时域滤波收敛极快。

    • 用一张图理解这块 3D 纹理的寻址：xy 平面按屏幕坐标取模，帧号沿 z 轴推进，每帧取一个切片：

    用法和 2D 蓝噪声一样，只是寻址多一维：

    float theta = texelFetch(stbnTex,    ivec3(ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) % size, frameIndex % depth), 0).r * 6.2831853;

    定位：有时域管线的现代引擎首选，代价几乎可以忽略，收益直接反映在 TAA 收敛速度上。

    3.6 黄金比率与低差异序列（时域去相关的数学优雅版）

    不想带纹理？可以用加性递归低差异序列直接在 shader 里算时域抖动。

    一维版本就是黄金比率序列。黄金比率 phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2 ≈ 1.618 是「最无理的数」，用它做步长取小数部分，得到的序列永不重复、永不聚集：

    二维推广是 Martin Roberts 的 R2 序列（The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quasirandom Sequences）：取塑性常数 psi ≈ 1.324718（方程 x³ = x + 1 的实根），令

    一个常见且好用的组合是给 IGN 加时域动画：让 IGN 的输出随帧叠加一个黄金比 / R2 步长的偏移，使空间上的规则图案每帧平移，TAA 下迅速收敛（Jimenez 在原演讲里用的是逐帧加一个黄金比偏移，这里用 R2 常数是同一思路的二维推广）：

    float animatedIGN(vec2 pixel, int frame){    const float r2 = 0.7548776662;    frame = frame % 64;              // 防浮点精度衰减    return fract(ign(pixel) + float(frame) * r2);}

    另一类低差异序列（Halton、Sobol）更多出现在路径追踪和上采样抖动（如 TAA 的 Halton(2,3) 相机 jitter），思路相同：用数学上保证均匀且不重复的序列替代随机。

    四、横向对比

    算法作用层频谱特性时间稳定性运行时成本典型适用场景
    泊松盘采样①采样核定 taps 位置—离线预生成，免费一切软阴影/PCSS 的 taps 布局
    fract-sin / 白噪声②抖动源全频段，低频差逐帧闪烁几条 ALU快速原型、有时域累积兜底
    Wang Hash②抖动源同白噪声（质量更稳）逐帧闪烁整数 ALU需要高质量随机种子的场合
    IGN②抖动源中高频，低频较少静态稳定约 1 次 MAD无纹理预算 + 有 TAA
    Bayer / 棋盘格②抖动源/欠采样规则高频稳定（翻转依赖 TAA）免费半分辨率采样、复古风格
    蓝噪声 BNDS②抖动源纯高频，单帧最优静态稳定1 次纹理 fetch无累积前向渲染的质量天花板
    STBN②抖动源空间+时间双高频时域收敛最快1 次 3D fetch现代 TAA 管线首选
    黄金比率 / R2②时域序列时域均匀无重复累积收敛几条 ALU给 IGN 加动画、相机 jitter
    Halton / Sobol②时域序列低差异、可收敛累积收敛免费TAA jitter、蒙特卡洛积分

    五、实战选型建议

  • 先确定采样核：taps 用离线生成的泊松盘，别用均匀网格，这一步白捡质量。
  • 没有 TAA 的前向管线：上蓝噪声纹理（BNDS），单帧观感最好，一次 fetch 换「看不见条纹」。
  • 有 TAA 的现代管线：STBN 一步到位；不想带纹理就用 IGN + R2 时域动画，成本几乎为零，收敛略逊于 STBN 但完全够用。
  • 需要砍采样量：棋盘格 + 帧奇偶翻转，让 TAA 把另一半样本补回来。
  • 别忘了旋转：第②层的输出通常作为 θ 去旋转泊松盘（见 2.2 节），而不是直接当 shadow offset 用——旋转保持核内相关性、破坏像素间相关性，这是去 banding 的关键直觉。
  • 帧序号记得取模（如 % 64），否则大帧号下浮点精度会让低差异序列退化。

    • 六、参考资料

  • Jorge Jimenez, Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, SIGGRAPH 2014（IGN 出处）
  • Eric Heitz, Laurent Belcour et al., A Low-Discrepancy Sampler that Distributes Monte Carlo Errors as a Blue Noise in Screen Space, SIGGRAPH 2019（屏幕空间蓝噪声误差分布 / 样本重排）
  • Alan Wolfe et al. (NVIDIA), Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks, EGSR 2022（STBN 3D 纹理，本文 3.5 节所指）
  • Robert Ulichney, Void-and-Cluster Method for Dither Array Generation, 1993（蓝噪声生成）
  • Martin Roberts, The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quasirandom Sequences（R1/R2 序列）
  • Robert Bridson, Fast Poisson Disk Sampling in Arbitrary Dimensions, SIGGRAPH 2007 Sketches
  • Christoph Peters, Moments in Graphics 博客（免费 STBN/蓝噪声纹理资源）
item.content:encoded:
一句话：抖动不是为了好看，而是把低频条纹换成能被 TAA 与时域累积抹掉的高频噪声——选错抖动，降噪器也救不回来。

要点：

  • 问题不是噪声而是 banding：PCF/PCSS 只有 16–32 次采样去逼近连续积分，所有像素共用同一组偏移时，相邻像素遮挡值完全相同，形成肉眼可见的条纹
  • 先分清两个正交概念：采样核形状（所有像素共用，均匀网格 / 均匀圆盘 / 泊松盘…）与逐像素抖动序列，混为一谈是最常见的设计错误
  • 抖动序列从白噪声一路讲到时空蓝噪声，给出原理、公式与可直接抄的代码，最后附对比表与实战选型建议

为什么值得看：软阴影的质量上限往往由抖动序列决定，而它又是最容易被随手糊一个 rand() 的地方。PCF/PCSS 实现要复现或调优时，可以直接按这篇的对比表选序列，而不是凭感觉试。

中文摘要：做软阴影（PCF / PCSS）或任何有限次采样的效果时都会遇到同一个问题：采样点不够用。16–32 次采样去逼近连续积分，若所有像素共用同一组采样偏移，结果不是噪声而是一条条肉眼可见的带状条纹，因为同一光源下相邻像素算出的遮挡值完全相同。解决思路很统一：给每个像素施加不同的抖动，把规则的 banding 打散成高频噪声——高频噪声对人眼更友好，而且能被 TAA、时域累积或降噪器抹掉，条纹则不能。文章先区分两个常被混淆的正交概念：采样核形状与逐像素抖动序列，再系统梳理从白噪声到蓝噪声、时空蓝噪声的抖动算法，给出原理、公式与可直接使用的代码，最后给出对比表和按场景的选型建议。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：公众号·游戏AI编程与图形渲染（中文）

原文发布：2026-10-15

本期推送：2026-10-24

做软阴影（PCF / PCSS）或者任何有限次采样的效果时，都会遇到同一个问题：采样点不够用。

比如 PCSS 里你只能用 16~32 次采样去逼近一个连续积分，如果所有像素都用同一组采样偏移，结果不是噪声，而是一条一条肉眼可见的带状条纹（banding）——因为同一个光源下相邻像素算出来的遮挡值完全相同。

解决思路非常统一：给每个像素施加一个不同的抖动（dither），把空间上规则的 banding 打散成高频噪声。噪声虽然难看，但它有两个好处：

  • 高频噪声对人眼远比低频条纹「友好」；
  • 噪声可以被 TAA / 时域累积 / 降噪器轻松抹掉，而条纹不能。

    • 下面这张图就是全文的直觉起点——同一条连续的半影梯度，欠采样后变成刺眼的条纹，而抖动把条纹换成了人眼更能容忍、且可被时域滤波抹掉的噪声：

    这篇文章把阴影采样里常用的抖动算法系统梳理一遍，给出原理、公式和可直接抄的代码，最后给一张对比表和实战选型建议。

    先用一张流程图把整条采样链路串起来，后面每一节都对应图里的一个方块：

    一、先分清两个正交的概念

    很多人会把「泊松盘采样」和「蓝噪声抖动」混为一谈，其实它们作用在完全不同的环节。一个带抖动的阴影采样器，由两部分组成：

    ① 采样核的形状（所有像素共用）：n 个 tap 在圆盘/平面上怎么摆。

  • 均匀网格：最差，方向性明显；
  • 均匀圆盘（极坐标均匀）：一般；
  • 泊松盘（Poisson Disk）：任意两点距离有下限，覆盖均匀无聚集，是软阴影采样核的事实标准。

    • ② 逐像素的去相关源（每像素不同）：怎么让相邻像素用「同一核的不同旋转/不同排列」。

  • 哈希白噪声、Wang Hash；
  • IGN（Interleaved Gradient Noise）；
  • Bayer 有序抖动 / 棋盘格；
  • 蓝噪声纹理（BNDS）、STBN；
  • 黄金比率 / 低差异序列（时域）。

    • 常见组合是：泊松盘定 taps 位置 + 每像素一个随机角度 θ，把整盘 taps 旋转 θ：

    所以下面讲算法时请注意它属于哪一层：泊松盘是第①层，其余全是第②层。用一张图把两层的分工固定下来：

    二、采样核层：泊松盘采样（Poisson Disk）

    2.1 为什么用它当采样核

    软阴影本质是圆盘（或球面）上的积分，tap 之间如果距离太近就是浪费——它们采到的信息高度相关。泊松盘约束任意两点最小距离 ≥ r，让有限 taps 的覆盖最均匀。下图左边是均匀网格（明显的横竖方向性 + 圆盘边缘浪费），右边是泊松盘（点距均匀、无聚集）：

    经典生成算法：

  • Dart Throwing：随机撒点，违反最小距离就丢弃，简单但慢；
  • Best-Candidate：每轮生成 k 个候选，保留离现有点集最远的那个，质量接近 dart throwing，快得多；
  • Bridson 算法（2007）：用背景网格加速，线性时间，是离线生成的常用选择。

    • 实际项目里不需要运行时生成——离线生成一次，硬编码成常量数组：

    // 16 tap 泊松盘（示意，实际数值由离线 best-candidate 生成）const vec2 poissonDisk[16] = vec2[](    vec2(-0.9420, -0.3993), vec2( 0.9455,  0.7689),    vec2(-0.0941, -0.9293), vec2( 0.3449,  0.2938),    vec2(-0.9158,  0.4577), vec2(-0.8154, -0.8791),    vec2(-0.3827,  0.2767), vec2( 0.9748,  0.7564),    vec2( 0.4432, -0.9751), vec2( 0.5374, -0.4737),    vec2(-0.2649, -0.4184), vec2( 0.7919,  0.1909),    vec2(-0.2418,  0.9970), vec2(-0.1998, -0.0733),    vec2( 0.1715, -0.4562), vec2(-0.2911,  0.6493));

    2.2 配合逐像素旋转去 banding

    float ShadowPCF(sampler2DShadow shadowMap, vec3 shadowCoord, float radius, float theta){    float s = sin(theta), c = cos(theta);    mat2 rot = mat2(c, -s, s, c);    float sum = 0.0;    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {        vec2 offset = rot * poissonDisk[i] * radius;        sum += texture(shadowMap, vec3(shadowCoord.xy + offset, shadowCoord.z));    }    return sum / 16.0;}

    θ 从哪里来？这正是第②层各算法的分工。

    三、逐像素抖动层：六种主流方案

    3.1 白噪声与哈希：最朴素的起点

    fract-sin 哈希（GPU 上最常用的伪随机）：

    float rand(vec2 p) {    return fract(sin(dot(p, vec2(12.9898, 78.233))) * 43758.5453);}float theta = rand(gl_FragCoord.xy) * 6.2831853;

    Wang Hash（整数域，质量好于 fract-sin，无精度问题）：

    uint wang_hash(uint seed){    seed = (seed ^ 61u) ^ (seed >> 16u);    seed *= 9u;    seed = seed ^ (seed >> 4u);    seed *= 0x27d4eb2du;    seed = seed ^ (seed >> 15u);    return seed;}// 用法：theta = float(wang_hash(uint(gl_FragCoord.x) * 1973u//            ^ uint(gl_FragCoord.y) * 9277u)) * (1.0/4294967296.0) * 6.2831853;

    问题：白噪声的频谱是全频段平坦的，包含大量低频能量。低频噪声 = 大块的明暗斑块，时域滤波很难收敛干净，视觉上就是「擦不掉的脏」。这正是后面所有算法要解决的问题。

    下面这张对比图是理解整篇文章的关键。上排是白噪声，右侧频谱图中心（低频区）能量很强；下排是蓝噪声，空间上看更「均匀细碎」，频谱中心是一个明显的空洞——低频能量被彻底抽走，只留高频。人眼对低频最敏感，所以蓝噪声「看起来」误差最小：

    一个常见误区：Wang Hash 只是「更好的白噪声生成器」，它并不改善噪声的频谱形状。要改善频谱，得换空间分布结构。

    3.2 Interleaved Gradient Noise（IGN）

    来自 Jorge Jimenez（Activision）的 Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty（SIGGRAPH 2014）。核心观察：有规律的、梯度交错的小结构噪声，比白噪声更容易被 TAA 吸收。

    公式极其简洁：

    float ign(vec2 pixel){    return fract(52.9829189 * fract(0.06711056 * pixel.x                                  + 0.00583715 * pixel.y));}float theta = ign(gl_FragCoord.xy) * 6.2831853;

    特点：

  • 零纹理、零状态、一个 MAD 指令级别，几乎是免费的；
  • 空间上是规则的梯度交错图案，低频能量比白噪声少；
  • 和 TAA 配合极佳（CoD 的 SSR、体积雾都靠它）；
  • 单帧静态看会有轻微规则纹理感，动起来或累积后消失。

    • 3.3 Bayer 有序抖动与棋盘格

    Bayer 矩阵是最经典的有序抖动，4x4 版本（值除以 16 归一化）：

    特点是「最大化已点亮像素之间的距离」，频谱上能量被推到高频，类似粗糙版的蓝噪声。优点是完全确定、可平铺；缺点是规则图案在静态画面上能被看出来（复古抖动风格）。

    棋盘格（checkerboard）是 2x2 Bayer 的特例，但它的用法不太一样——不是拿来生成 θ，而是拿来砍采样量：

  • 棋盘格的一种颜色采「样本集合 A」，另一种颜色采「样本集合 B」，每像素成本减半；
  • 帧奇偶时间翻转：偶数帧像素 (x+y) 为偶时采 A，奇数帧翻转采 B。两帧合起来每个像素都覆盖过 A 和 B，TAA 一累积就是全量采样：
    • bool parity = ((int(gl_FragCoord.x) + int(gl_FragCoord.y) + frameIndex) & 1) == 0;vec2 offset = rot * (parity ? tapsA[i] : tapsB[i]);

    这是「空间欠采样 + 时间补偿」的思路，在半分辨率阴影、半分辨率 AO 里非常常见。前提是你的 TAA 足够稳，否则翻转帧之间会闪。

    3.4 蓝噪声纹理（Blue Noise / BNDS）

    蓝噪声的定义是频谱上只有高频能量、低频区为空的噪声。人眼对低频敏感、对高频迟钝，所以同样的采样误差，按蓝噪声分布「看起来」最少。

    与 Bayer 的区别：Bayer 是规则周期图案，蓝噪声是无规则但满足最小距离约束的分布——可以把它理解成「抖动的泊松盘」。

  • 离线用 Void-and-Cluster（Ulichney 1993）算法生成，并做边缘回绕使其可无缝平铺；
  • 运行时一次纹理 fetch，按屏幕坐标取模寻址：
    • float theta = texelFetch(blueNoiseTex,    ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) % textureSize(blueNoiseTex, 0), 0).r * 6.2831853;
  • 工程界有现成的免费高质量蓝噪声纹理（如 Christoph Peters 的 Moments in Graphics 博客提供的 STBN/BNDS 资源），Unity HDRP、Unreal 引擎内部也都是直接内置蓝噪声纹理。

    • 定位：第②层的「单帧质量天花板」，代价是一张纹理。没有时域累积的纯前向渲染里，蓝噪声通常是最佳选择。

    3.5 时空蓝噪声（STBN）

    蓝噪声只优化了空间维。如果渲染是逐帧变化 + 时域累积的，理想情况是：每一帧在空间上是蓝噪声，同一像素在时间维也去相关。

    这里要澄清一个常见的出处混淆。业界有两条相关但不同的路线：

  • Heitz & Belcour, SIGGRAPH 2019（A Low-Discrepancy Sampler that Distributes Monte Carlo Errors as a Blue Noise in Screen Space）：思路是逐像素重排采样序列，让蒙特卡洛误差在屏幕空间上呈蓝噪声分布，本质是「样本置换 + 空间蓝噪声掩码」，并不是一张 3D 纹理。
  • Wolfe et al. (NVIDIA), EGSR 2022（Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks，即通常说的 STBN 纹理）：把蓝噪声掩码直接做成 3D 纹理，xy 是屏幕空间，z 是帧序号——下面代码里 
    stbnTex
     用的就是这套。

    • 以 3D 纹理版 STBN 为例，它的两个核心性质是：

  • 每个 z 切片单独看都是一张合法的空间蓝噪声；
  • 沿 z 轴（时间维）看，同一像素在相邻帧的取值也满足蓝噪声关系，误差互相「错开」，时域滤波收敛极快。

    • 用一张图理解这块 3D 纹理的寻址：xy 平面按屏幕坐标取模，帧号沿 z 轴推进，每帧取一个切片：

    用法和 2D 蓝噪声一样，只是寻址多一维：

    float theta = texelFetch(stbnTex,    ivec3(ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) % size, frameIndex % depth), 0).r * 6.2831853;

    定位：有时域管线的现代引擎首选，代价几乎可以忽略，收益直接反映在 TAA 收敛速度上。

    3.6 黄金比率与低差异序列（时域去相关的数学优雅版）

    不想带纹理？可以用加性递归低差异序列直接在 shader 里算时域抖动。

    一维版本就是黄金比率序列。黄金比率 phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2 ≈ 1.618 是「最无理的数」，用它做步长取小数部分，得到的序列永不重复、永不聚集：

    二维推广是 Martin Roberts 的 R2 序列（The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quasirandom Sequences）：取塑性常数 psi ≈ 1.324718（方程 x³ = x + 1 的实根），令

    一个常见且好用的组合是给 IGN 加时域动画：让 IGN 的输出随帧叠加一个黄金比 / R2 步长的偏移，使空间上的规则图案每帧平移，TAA 下迅速收敛（Jimenez 在原演讲里用的是逐帧加一个黄金比偏移，这里用 R2 常数是同一思路的二维推广）：

    float animatedIGN(vec2 pixel, int frame){    const float r2 = 0.7548776662;    frame = frame % 64;              // 防浮点精度衰减    return fract(ign(pixel) + float(frame) * r2);}

    另一类低差异序列（Halton、Sobol）更多出现在路径追踪和上采样抖动（如 TAA 的 Halton(2,3) 相机 jitter），思路相同：用数学上保证均匀且不重复的序列替代随机。

    四、横向对比

    算法作用层频谱特性时间稳定性运行时成本典型适用场景
    泊松盘采样①采样核定 taps 位置—离线预生成，免费一切软阴影/PCSS 的 taps 布局
    fract-sin / 白噪声②抖动源全频段，低频差逐帧闪烁几条 ALU快速原型、有时域累积兜底
    Wang Hash②抖动源同白噪声（质量更稳）逐帧闪烁整数 ALU需要高质量随机种子的场合
    IGN②抖动源中高频，低频较少静态稳定约 1 次 MAD无纹理预算 + 有 TAA
    Bayer / 棋盘格②抖动源/欠采样规则高频稳定（翻转依赖 TAA）免费半分辨率采样、复古风格
    蓝噪声 BNDS②抖动源纯高频，单帧最优静态稳定1 次纹理 fetch无累积前向渲染的质量天花板
    STBN②抖动源空间+时间双高频时域收敛最快1 次 3D fetch现代 TAA 管线首选
    黄金比率 / R2②时域序列时域均匀无重复累积收敛几条 ALU给 IGN 加动画、相机 jitter
    Halton / Sobol②时域序列低差异、可收敛累积收敛免费TAA jitter、蒙特卡洛积分

    五、实战选型建议

  • 先确定采样核：taps 用离线生成的泊松盘，别用均匀网格，这一步白捡质量。
  • 没有 TAA 的前向管线：上蓝噪声纹理（BNDS），单帧观感最好，一次 fetch 换「看不见条纹」。
  • 有 TAA 的现代管线：STBN 一步到位；不想带纹理就用 IGN + R2 时域动画，成本几乎为零，收敛略逊于 STBN 但完全够用。
  • 需要砍采样量：棋盘格 + 帧奇偶翻转，让 TAA 把另一半样本补回来。
  • 别忘了旋转：第②层的输出通常作为 θ 去旋转泊松盘（见 2.2 节），而不是直接当 shadow offset 用——旋转保持核内相关性、破坏像素间相关性，这是去 banding 的关键直觉。
  • 帧序号记得取模（如 % 64），否则大帧号下浮点精度会让低差异序列退化。

    • 六、参考资料

  • Jorge Jimenez, Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, SIGGRAPH 2014（IGN 出处）
  • Eric Heitz, Laurent Belcour et al., A Low-Discrepancy Sampler that Distributes Monte Carlo Errors as a Blue Noise in Screen Space, SIGGRAPH 2019（屏幕空间蓝噪声误差分布 / 样本重排）
  • Alan Wolfe et al. (NVIDIA), Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks, EGSR 2022（STBN 3D 纹理，本文 3.5 节所指）
  • Robert Ulichney, Void-and-Cluster Method for Dither Array Generation, 1993（蓝噪声生成）
  • Martin Roberts, The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quasirandom Sequences（R1/R2 序列）
  • Robert Bridson, Fast Poisson Disk Sampling in Arbitrary Dimensions, SIGGRAPH 2007 Sketches
  • Christoph Peters, Moments in Graphics 博客（免费 STBN/蓝噪声纹理资源）

item.title: EGGHead：给固定的高斯预算，按语义区域分配，单次前向就出可驱动的人头 ｜ EGGHead: Efficient Generalizable Gaussian Heads from a Single Image
item.description:
一句话：高斯头部的开销取决于光栅化多少个高斯、以及准备头部要多久；按语义区域分配预算，两者一起降。

要点：

  • 核心是一个高斯分配算法：在固定预算下，把高斯按语义区域分给头部不同部位，用更少的高斯保住表征力
  • 单次前向完成，避免了 Gaussian 头部方法常见的漫长 enrollment（逐个优化准备）时间
  • 在重建质量、新视角合成与渲染速度三方面都超过此前的单图人脸建模方法

为什么值得看：数字人进游戏或实时应用，卡的是「每个角色准备多久」和「每帧光栅化多少高斯」。把预算分配显式做成算法，比无脑加高斯更适合放进资产流水线。

中文摘要：做照片级人头一直在表征力、效率与泛化性之间取舍：3DMM 这类网格方案渲染高效但表征力受限；NeRF 方案保真度高却牺牲效率；高斯泼溅想两头兼顾，但效率依旧取决于光栅化多少个高斯，而准备头部的 enrollment 时间往往很长。EGGHead 提出一种高斯分配算法：在固定高斯预算下，把高斯高效分配到头部各语义区域，在尽量不影响表征力的前提下减少所需高斯数量。整个模型单次前向即可出结果，在重建质量、新视角合成与渲染速度上都优于此前单图人脸建模方法。

EGGHead: Efficient Generalizable Gaussian Heads from a Single Image

Abstract

Creating photorealistic human heads typically involves trade-offs between representation power, efficiency, and generalizability. Traditional mesh-based solutions relying on 3DMMs generally sacrifice representation power but are efficient to render. On the other hand, NeRF-based methods improve representation power and fidelity while sacrificing efficiency. Gaussian splatting methods attempt to resolve these trade-offs by offering both high representation power and efficiency with real-time rendering. However, their efficiency nonetheless depends on the number of rasterized Gaussians, and the time needed to optimize and prepare the head (the enrollment time) is often high. In light of this, we propose EGGHead, which introduces a novel Gaussian allocation algorithm that efficiently assigns Gaussians to the head’s semantic regions given a fixed Gaussian budget. Our algorithm reduces the number of Gaussians needed while minimizing the impact on representation power. EGGHead operates in a single forward pass and outperforms previous single-image face modeling methods in reconstruction quality, novel view synthesis, and rendering speeds.

1 Introduction

Modeling photorealistic human heads has received widespread attention from the computer vision and graphics communities. It has a wide array of applications, including movie production [31], digital humans in AR/VR [70, 90, 75, 25], and downstream tasks in the face domain [59, 58]. There are several important axes to consider when designing a head reconstruction method, including representation power, the efficiency of the 3D representation, and data requirements. An ideal method produces a high-quality head that captures fine identity details, enables real-time generation and novel view synthesis, and requires minimal data.

Traditional head representation methods adopt mesh-based approaches that rely on 3DMMs [10] to model the face. Although generally efficient to rasterize and render, and despite a plethora of single-image based methods [86, 83, 53, 84, 6], these 3D representations generally lack high representation power due to reliance on PCA bases, carrying over artifacts from intrinsic decomposition into rendering. The follow-up methods [70, 71, 38, 25, 97, 37] relied instead on the implicit NeRF [65] representation, which allowed for higher representation power thanks to per-pixel raytracing, the ability to model view-specific texture variations, and the volumetric rendering design. However, NeRF-based methods sacrifice efficiency since the raytracing inference stage is often costly. More recently, the face modeling community has favored mesh-driven 3D Gaussian Splatting [45] (3D-GS): a hybrid explicit-implicit representation that allows for both high fidelity and real-time rendering.

Gaussian Splatting, however, is not without limitations. While considered a representation that enables real-time rendering, the efficiency is still affected by the number of Gaussians used to represent the head. In practice, high-quality Gaussian heads require a large number of Gaussians to capture fine geometric and appearance details. Reducing the number of Gaussians is thus an important priority, but if done naively will simply reduce the head’s fidelity. To address this trade-off between fidelity and efficiency, we propose a novel Gaussian Allocation Module (GAM), which efficiently allocates a fixed budget of M Gaussians while minimizing the impact on the head’s fidelity.

Moreover, 3D-GS traditionally relies on monocular or multi-view image/video inputs, is trained per subject instead of being generalizable, and requires an expensive optimization for each subject ranging from a few minutes to one hour [73, 16, 90]. GPS-Gaussian [96] resolves some of these limitations by producing a generalizable method that takes a stereo pair of images as input and predicts Gaussian attributes. However, it requires a monocular video as input, since the method depends on the nearest-neighbor stereo pair for each queried viewpoint. Moreover, it makes the naive assumption of assigning one Gaussian to each pixel, which will naturally reduce the rendering speed. We instead reduce this requirement from a monocular video to a single image while also proposing a generalizable method given one image as input. Our novel GAM improves rendering speed by allocating Gaussians over semantic regions rather than on a per-pixel basis, achieving high fidelity with fewer Gaussians. In addition, we employ Voronoi tessellation [11] to guide Gaussian attribute computation in a single-view setting with sparse Gaussians. Finally, we introduce a lightweight, network-free Face Symmetry Module to render occluded face regions, avoiding expensive post-processing networks and diffusion-based multi-view generation during inference.

Our contributions are thus as follows:

\diamond We propose EGGHead, a single-image and generalizable Gaussian head model that outperforms existing approaches in rendering quality and speed while achieving competitive enrollment time.

\diamond We introduce a Gaussian Allocation Module (GAM) that allocates Gaussians under a fixed budget with minimal impact, employ Voronoi tessellation to guide Gaussian shape computation in a single-view setting with sparse Gaussians, and incorporate a lightweight Face Symmetry Module to improve head completeness without relying on additional networks.

\diamond We demonstrate superior head representation capabilities and fidelity among single-image head reconstruction methods, both quantitatively and qualitatively.

2 Related Work

Face Modeling.

Existing 3D face representations include explicit mesh-based methods [84, 57, 83, 56, 39, 58, 86, 53, 6, 77, 59, 8, 9, 85], implicit NeRF-based [65] methods [25, 74, 70, 26, 5, 29, 71, 27, 89, 97, 37, 13, 94, 38], diffusion models conditioned with 3D priors [21, 42], 3D-aware GANs that incorporate triplane representations [2, 52, 14, 30, 22, 91, 79, 76, 80, 19, 93, 34], and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3D-GS) [45, 75, 17, 73, 64, 16, 78, 90, 15, 81, 87, 49]. Mesh-based 3DMMs [10] enable fast rendering but are limited in fidelity by their PCA basis. NeRF-based methods improve fidelity through view-dependent neural rendering, but require costly ray sampling. 3D-GS offers high-quality real-time rendering, yet its efficiency depends on the number of Gaussians and still requires seconds to minutes of per-subject enrollment. To address this, we introduce EGGHead, a generalizable model that effectively reduces the Gaussian budget.

Generalizable Gaussian Splatting.

Although 3D-GS is traditionally optimized per scene or subject, generalizable 3D-GS methods have recently gained attention. GPS-Gaussian [96] synthesizes unseen identities but assigns one Gaussian per pixel, limiting efficiency. GAGAvatar [17] predicts Gaussians from a single image using FLAME [55] and dual lifting, but its additional neural renderer may compromise identity consistency. Diffusion-based methods [82, 63] achieve high quality but rely on costly multi-view generation. In contrast, EGGHead uses GAM to merge Gaussians in fidelity-insensitive regions, avoiding dense per-pixel allocation, and multi-view generation.

Efficient Gaussian Splatting.

Several methods improve the efficiency of 3D-GS by compressing Gaussian parameters or pruning low-impact Gaussians. Compression methods [54, 67, 66] reduce storage and rendering costs by removing parameter redundancy, while pruning-based methods [23, 28, 69] reduce the Gaussian count. However, they still rely on costly multi-view optimization. In contrast, our GAM operates from a single image and directly allocates a compact set of Gaussians.

Symmetry in Face Modeling.

Face symmetry is a strong prior that preserves the naturally symmetrical structure of human faces, especially in the ill-posed single-image setting where occluded regions rely on face priors to be properly reconstructed.
